answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tending trust like a garden rather than handing it out. A newcomer plants one verifiable service task in a shared bed and earns standing only as unrelated peers confirm real work, the way a comet leaves a bright trail that cannot be faked twice. Each completed task issues a one-time work receipt that echoes across independent witnesses, and duplicate echoes from the same hand are discarded. If fraud is found, the whole bed is uprooted and the sponsor loses their stake, so growing many fake identities costs far more than it can ever earn.
